goal: Draft a detailed but concise Russian learning card about Intel 80386, with distinct answer intents rather than paraphrased definitions.

source_documents.locator: October 17, 1985, Raising the Bar with the 386
facts: Intel introduced 80386 in 1985; the historical timeline dates the entry October 17.
The cited initial product had a 16 MHz clock and 275,000 transistors; do not generalize these numbers to every 386 variant.
Intel386 was the first 32-bit processor in Intel's IA-32 family, with 32-bit registers for operands and addressing.
It retained the lower 16-bit register portions for backward compatibility and provided virtual-8086 mode.
Its 32-bit address bus supports up to 4 GiB physical address space.
It supports segmented and flat memory models, and paging with fixed 4-KiB pages.
